quantum_strategy: Keystone AI + Quantum Factory (April 2026), a statewide network of the seven R1 research universities with Commonwealth support; House Communications and Technology Committee informational meeting on quantum (Aug. 11, 2026); no quantum statute
key_institutions: Carnegie Mellon, Drexel, Lehigh, Penn State, Temple, Penn, Pitt; Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center
equipment_language: Equipment used to "outfit, operate or benefit a computer data center," including mechanical equipment and refrigerant piping (Department of Revenue guidelines)
facility_qualification: Unlikely: $75M or $100M investment and 25 or 45 jobs; qualified tenants must commit to at least 100 kW per month
large_load_threshold: 50 MW individually or 100 MW aggregate (PUC model tariff)
facility_reporting_rule: Act 21 of 2026 covers facilities predominantly housing servers with peak demand of 10 MW or more; a quantum facility would meet neither test
pqc_it_standard: No. The Office of Administration's Encryption Policy (effective Dec. 30, 2025) has no quantum language; its next review is due December 2026.
pqc_encryption_standard: FIPS 140-2 implementation guidance; conformance with NIST's Cryptographic Module Validation Program
pqc_utility_regulator: The PUC's June 2026 proposed cybersecurity rule for utilities has no quantum language.
pqc_public_discussion: At the House Communications and Technology Committee's Aug. 11, 2026 informational meeting, a witness testified that state agencies "should already be actively preparing for this transition."

quantum_strategy: Virginia Quantum Hub at George Mason University (September 2026); Joint Commission on Technology and Science quantum study (2025); no quantum statute
state_funding_confirmed: $3,684,912 GO Virginia Region 7 grant for the Virginia Quantum Hub
key_institutions: George Mason University, Virginia Tech, Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation
equipment_language: "Computer equipment or enabling software ... including ... other enabling hardware, including chillers and backup generators" (Va. Code § 58.1-609.3(18)); Tax Commissioner Ruling 23-92 extends to HVAC and cooling towers
facility_qualification: Unlikely: $150M investment plus jobs under a VEDP memorandum of understanding
facility_reporting_rule: No facility-level reporting rule; the SCC's annual report aggregates data center figures from utilities
pqc_it_standard: No quantum language found in VITA's SEC530 Information Security Standard (rev. June 17, 2025). A 2019 VITA technical brief (guidance, not a standard) says agencies "should identify and inventory dependency on quantum-vulnerable cryptographic algorithms."
pqc_strategy: A 2025 Joint Commission on Technology and Science report asks how the state could encourage migration to quantum-resistant encryption; it makes no recommendations.
pqc_procurement: A vendor's announcement of a $285 million VITA cybersecurity services contract (Dec. 2025) says it will support "VITA's post-quantum cryptography initiatives" (vendor announcement; contract terms not public).
pqc_utility_regulator: The SCC's November 2025 report on utility cybersecurity has no quantum language.
pqc_public_discussion: VITA's August 2026 information security conference included a session on building quantum-resilient systems.

quantum_strategy: Ohio Institute for Quantum Computing Research, Talent, and Commercialization (Miami University with Cleveland Clinic), funded in the FY2026-27 budget; IBM Quantum System One installed at Cleveland Clinic in 2023; no quantum statute
state_funding_confirmed: $7,000,000 in the enacted FY2026-27 budget (HB 96); $14M was originally proposed
equipment_language: Property used "to conduct a computer data center business, including equipment cooling systems" (Ohio Rev. Code § 122.175)
facility_qualification: Unlikely: must be a computer data center business providing electronic information services, with $100M investment and $1.5M payroll; research use would not qualify
pqc_legislation: HB 650 would create a Frontier Technologies and Quantum Commission to study security and infrastructure resilience, with a report due Dec. 31, 2026; passed the House 92–0 on Mar. 4, 2026 and is in Senate committee. It does not address encryption.

quantum_strategy: Capital of Quantum initiative (January 2025), a public-private partnership seeking $1 billion in investment; December 2024 executive order named quantum a priority industry; DARPA benchmarking hub agreement (April 2025)
state_funding_confirmed: FY2026 proposal: $27.5M initial investment; FY2027 budget: $54M ($20M for IonQ's headquarters, $22M for UMD quantum programs and testbeds, $12M for faculty and technical experts)
key_institutions: University of Maryland, IonQ, Applied Research Laboratory for Intelligence and Security
equipment_language: "Computer equipment or enabling software ... including servers, routers, connections, and other enabling hardware" (Md. Tax-General § 11-239)
facility_qualification: Possible: $2M (Tier 1 area) or $5M investment and five qualified positions; whether a quantum facility counts as a data center is untested
quantum_specific_tax_incentive: None in tax law; support comes through appropriations and grants
pqc_it_standard: Yes, as a preference. MD-STD-318-SC-01 (Feb. 18, 2026) gives "preference ... to those designed to resist emerging post-quantum threats" and requires agencies to plan for cryptographic agility; agencies have 18 months to implement the new policy suite.
pqc_crypto_inventory: No. Asset inventories cover hardware, software and data, not cryptography.
pqc_strategy: The 2025 IT Master Plan extends the state's security architecture to quantum computing.
pqc_legislation: Chapter 628 of 2025 directs the Maryland Cybersecurity Council to "assess and address" risks from quantum computing.
pqc_encryption_standard: FIPS 140-3 (FIPS 140-2 modules allowed until their retirement on Sept. 21, 2026)
pqc_utility_regulator: None identified; the 2023 Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Act has no quantum language.
pqc_public_discussion: A Maryland Cybersecurity Council subcommittee raised quantum preparation as a possible agenda topic (Feb. 2026).

quantum_strategy: No state-level quantum action identified; activity is led by Georgia Tech, including its Quantum Applications Research Center (October 2026) and the Georgia Tech Research Institute's role in DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative
key_institutions: Georgia Tech, Georgia Tech Research Institute
equipment_language: Equipment used to "generate or provide constant delivery of power, environmental conditioning, air cooling" for computer equipment (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-12-2-.117)
facility_qualification: Unlikely: county-tiered minimums of $25M to $250M plus jobs
pqc_it_standard: No. GTA's Cryptographic Controls standard (SS-08-040, last reviewed Dec. 1, 2024) has no quantum language.
pqc_strategy: GTA's 2030 Enterprise IT Strategic Vision (April 2026) lists a long-term priority to "integrate quantum-resistant cryptography and long-term security planning."
